sentences.text: Agustinia is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that contains only one known species, Agustinia ligabuei. This animal was a quadrupedal herbivore, sharing a basic body plan with other large plant-eating dinosaurs of its time.
The animal is known only from fragmentary remains, including vertebrae from the back, hips, and tail, as well as parts of the lower hind limb such as a fibula, tibia, and five metatarsals.
A recovered fibula, also known as a perone bone, measures approximately 895 mm in length.
Based on the length of this single bone, scientists estimate the creature reached about 15 meters in total length.
The genus name Agustinia honors Agustín Martinelli, a student who discovered the skeleton during an excavation. The name was formally proposed in a major work published in 1999.
Jose Bonaparte first described the genus in that same year, and the single species was named in honor of philanthropist Dr. Giancarlo Ligabue, who funded the expedition.

D'emic et al. (2009) classified Agustinia as Neosauropoda incertae sedis due to a lack of diagnostic features. They concluded there were no diagnostic features to classify Agustinia within Diplodocoidea or Titanosauria, so they classified it as incertae sedis.

Some authors consider Agustinia a nomen dubium due to its fragmentary nature and lack of distinctive characteristics. It is debated whether Agustinia is a diplodocoid or titanosaurian based on conflicting vertebral features, as diplodocoids have compressed dorsal spines while titanosaurians have six sacral vertebrae. Agustinia is difficult to classify due to its fragmentary nature, which exposes traits of both diplodocoid and titanosaurian sauropods.
